text:
sara: Heads-up — Legal flagged a retention-exception request from a EU customer. They claim a contract clause requires us to keep a subset of user transcripts + derived embeddings for 13 months. They want a signed exception while they coordinate with their DPO. Can we outline the minimal controls we need to approve?

ajay: Thanks. Do we have the exact scope? Is it full transcripts or only redacted metadata + embeddings? Also which KMS is used for those snapshots?

sara: It's transcripts + embeddings for a cohort of users (approx 18k rows). Requested storage: S3 EU region; KMS key: projects/redwood/eu-keys/priv-emb-v2. They said no downstream sharing but want access for audits.

marta: from a privacy perspective we should insist on strict RBAC (auditor role read-only), TTL on derived embeddings, and proof of consent or contractual lawful basis. If Legal signs, we still need a technical mitigation plan to minimize surface area.

kyle: On the infra side: we can create a scoped S3 bucket with prefix access and a dedicated IAM role. But the tricky part is ensuring deletion propagation if they later request erasure. Snapshot and snapshot-s3-lifecycle need to be coordinated.

ajay: Two security items: 1) KMS key access must be restricted to a service-account with key-use only, and we need an audit path showing decrypt calls. 2) RBAC change request should be reviewed by infra and security — no broad team permissions.

sara: Request from Legal also asked to pause normal data minimization purge for that cohort until the exception expires. That's the part that concerns me.

marta: If we grant an exception, we should:  - require periodic revalidation (every 90 days)  - attach a retention-expiry tag to every object and ensure automated purge  - limit query surfaces (no embeddings served to model)

privacy-bot: AUTO: retention-exception #TICKET-2026-449 created by sara. Reminder: attach contract scan + DPO email to ticket.

ajay: Also, we recently discovered a vuln during snapshot retention audit — there was a misconfigured ACL on an older archive causing public-read on a small set of artifacts (no keys). We should add that to the risk assessment.

kyle: Right — that's the vuln triage. I dug the CloudTrail logs:

```
2026-03-19T11:12:03Z s3 PutObject acl=public-read bucket=redwood-archive prefix=backups/2024-11-12/part-003
2026-03-19T11:12:04Z iam CreatePolicy policy=allow-everyone-temp
```

This was from a long-deleted automation. We rotated the service-account and revoked the old policy. No evidence of exfil. Still need to document.

marta: For the retention-exception approval checklist I propose: 1) Contract + DPO approval 2) Scoped KMS key with limited principal list 3) RBAC review + just-in-time access for auditors 4) Automated labels + TTL 5) Incident rollback plan (how to erase if DSAR arrives) 6) Quarterly re-validation 7) Logging & export of KMS decrypt events to an immutable audit trail.

sara: Sounds good. Can we get a concrete RBAC change request template? Legal wants to see the controls before they sign.

ajay: I'll post a short template. Use a single role 'audit_reader_emb_v2' with least privilege: S3:GetObject on bucket prefix, KMS:Decrypt on key conditioned on tag exception=T2026-449, and explicit denies for S3:GetObject on objects tagged erase=true. Also add organization policy to prevent cross-account grants.

kyle: Implementation steps for infra: 1) create bucket + prefix 2) create KMS key policy limiting to service-account + security-admin 3) create IAM role and attach permission boundary 4) configure lifecycle rule for TTL 5) wire CloudTrail & Push to longterm audit. I can take 2 & 3, will need ajay for policy review.

privacy-bot: ACTION: assign kyle to infra task and ajay to security policy review.

marta: One more edge-case: DSAR deletion where embeddings are derived and stored elsewhere (vector DB). We must ensure a propagation plan: erase source transcripts, then regenerate embedding removal job that can match via provenance ids. If embeddings lack provenance, require a fallback manual redaction and note in Legal's exception.

sara: Good call. Legal — if you sign the exception we need a clause obligating them to provide provenance mapping on request. Otherwise we can't guarantee erasure.

ajay: I'll draft the RBAC JSON snippet here for Legal to review (minimal):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-priv-exceptions/2026/t2026-449/*"],"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"s3:ExistingObjectTag/exception":"T2026-449"}}},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":["arn:aws:kms:eu:123456:key/priv-emb-v2"],"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"kms:RequestTag/exception":"T2026-449"}}}
  ]
}
```
Note: explicit Deny for tag erase=true will be in org policy.

kyle: Thanks — I'll prototype infra in staging and submit a terraform PR to the infra repo. Will include lifecycle rule and CloudTrail sink.

marta: I'll draft the privacy addendum text requiring provenance and revalidation and attach it to the ticket.

sara: Great. Can we aim to have a first cut — PR + policy — by EOD Friday? That gives Legal something to sign over the weekend.

ajay: Agree. I'll do policy review and produce a short risk memo referencing the snapshot vuln and mitigations.

privacy-bot: REMINDER: TICKET-2026-449 next update due in 72 hours.

sara: thanks everyone. I'll update Legal and ping back here once they respond. :thumbsup:
